blocks.heading: LIKE = "similar to" / "for example"
blocks.rule: Like va seguido de un sustantivo o pronombre (noun phrase). Compara cosas que se parecen, pero que NO son lo mismo.
examples: He swims like a fish.
She sings like an angel.
I love outdoor sports, like climbing and kayaking. (informal)

blocks.heading: AS = función o papel real ("define")
blocks.rule: As indica lo que algo o alguien ES realmente: profesión, función, uso.
examples: She works as a nurse.
As your lawyer, I advise you not to sign.
The building was used as a hospital during the war.
blocks.tip: Like a lawyer = parece abogado (pero no lo es). As a lawyer = es abogado.

blocks.heading: AS = because / since
blocks.rule: En lugar de "because / since" podemos usar as para dar una razón.
examples: As it was raining, we stayed at home.
As I told you yesterday, the meeting has been cancelled.

blocks.heading: Comparaciones de igualdad: as ... as / the same as
blocks.rule: Para expresar igualdad usamos as + adj/adv + as, o the same (+ noun) + as. Nunca "the same like".
examples: Peter is as old as me.
My phone is the same as yours.
This jacket is the same price as that one.

blocks.heading: Define / regard / consider / know / describe + AS
blocks.rule: Estos verbos van seguidos de as para indicar cómo se ve o se clasifica a alguien o algo.
examples: Many people regard him as the best writer of his generation.
He was known as 'The Iron Man'.
The hotel was described as luxurious.
blocks.tip: Consider puede ir sin as: "They consider him (to be) a genius."

blocks.heading: SUCH AS = "for example"
blocks.rule: Such as introduce ejemplos. Es la opción formal (like es más informal).
examples: I enjoy water sports such as surfing and sailing.

blocks.heading: Verbos semi-copulativos (= to be): LOOK
blocks.rule: look + adjetivo · look like + noun phrase · look as if / as though + oración (= como si).
examples: You look tired.
He looks like my English teacher.
He looks as if he has studied a lot.
blocks.tip: Situación hipotética (no real) → pasado: "He looks as if he were a millionaire." (were para todas las personas en registro formal)

blocks.heading: Verbos semi-copulativos: SEEM (y sound / feel / smell / taste)
blocks.rule: seem + to be + adjetivo (sentimientos / impresiones) · seem like + noun phrase. Sound, feel, smell y taste funcionan igual que look.
examples: She seems to be upset today.
It seems like a good idea.
This soup tastes as if it's been in the fridge for a week.
It feels like silk.

blocks.heading: PREFER + V-ing + TO + V-ing
blocks.rule: Preferencia general. También prefer + noun + to + noun. ¡Nunca "than"!
examples: I prefer working as a plumber to working as a teacher.
She prefers tea to coffee.

blocks.heading: WOULD PREFER + to inf + RATHER THAN + inf (sin to)
blocks.rule: Preferencia concreta, en una situación específica. También would prefer + objeto + to inf.
examples: I would prefer to go to the park rather than go to the beach.
Would you prefer me to pick you up at the station?

blocks.heading: WOULD RATHER / WOULD SOONER + inf (sin to) + THAN + inf (sin to)
blocks.rule: Preferencia presente o futura. Mismo sujeto. Negativa: would rather not + inf.
examples: I would rather drive a car than drive a motorbike.
I'd sooner live in a city.
I'd rather not talk about it.

blocks.heading: WOULD RATHER + inf + AND NOT + inf
blocks.rule: Otra forma de contrastar dos opciones con would rather.
examples: She would rather travel alone and not with a group.

blocks.heading: WOULD + like / love / hate / prefer + TO inf
blocks.rule: "Me gustaría": deseo sobre una situación presente o futura.
examples: I would like to go to London.

blocks.heading: PASADO 1: WOULD + like / love / hate / prefer + TO HAVE + participio
blocks.rule: El deseo lo tienes AHORA, pero sobre algo que ya pasó. "Viendo las cosas ahora, preferiría que mi pasado fuera distinto." = Me gustaría haber estudiado (ahora).
examples: I would like to have studied Biology.
I would hate to have taken that exam without studying.

blocks.heading: PASADO 2: WOULD HAVE + liked / loved / hated / preferred + TO inf
blocks.rule: El deseo lo tenías EN EL PASADO: algo que querías hacer pero no pudiste o no lo hiciste. = Me habría / hubiera gustado hacerlo (ayer).
examples: I would have liked to study Biology.
I would have liked to meet you before you moved.

blocks.heading: WOULD RATHER / SOONER + HAVE + participio
blocks.rule: Preferencia sobre el pasado, del mismo sujeto. Equivale a would like + to have + participio.
examples: I would rather have lived in a city.
He'd sooner have kept the money than lent it.

blocks.heading: WOULD RATHER / SOONER + sujeto + PAST SIMPLE
blocks.rule: Queremos que OTRA persona haga (o no haga) algo en el presente o futuro. Negativa: would rather + sujeto + didn't.
examples: I would rather you bought a new phone.
I'd rather you didn't smoke in the house.

blocks.heading: WOULD RATHER / SOONER + sujeto + PAST PERFECT
blocks.rule: Preferencia de que otra persona hubiera hecho algo distinto en el pasado (arrepentimiento / queja).
examples: I would rather you had bought a new phone.
I'd rather you hadn't told anyone.

blocks.heading: IT'S (HIGH / ABOUT) TIME + sujeto + PAST SIMPLE
blocks.rule: Queremos que alguien haga algo "ya, ahora mismo" (suele tener tono de queja). Sin sujeto: It's time + to inf.
examples: It's high time you went to sleep.
It's about time we left.
It's time to go to bed.

blocks.heading: PAST SIMPLE: sujeto + verbo en pasado
blocks.rule: 1. Acciones que empezaron y terminaron en el pasado (yesterday, last + tiempo, tiempo + ago). 2. Hechos del pasado. 3. Rutinas / hábitos del pasado, con adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, often, rarely, seldom, never).
examples: She visited Paris last year.
Dinosaurs lived millions of years ago.
I often played football every weekend.

blocks.heading: USED TO + inf
blocks.rule: Rutinas o hábitos del pasado que YA NO ocurren en el presente. Sirve para acciones Y para estados (tener, vivir, gustar, ser...). Negativa: didn't use to.
examples: I used to play football every weekend.
We used to live in a small village.
I didn't use to like vegetables.
blocks.tip: No confundir con be / get used to + V-ing = estar acostumbrado / acostumbrarse.

blocks.heading: WOULD + inf (hábitos pasados)
blocks.rule: Rutinas del pasado que ya no ocurren, pero SOLO con acciones, nunca con estados. Con estados (like / love / hate / be / have / live...) solo podemos usar used to.
examples: When I was a child, I would climb trees every afternoon.
✗ I would have long hair. → ✓ I used to have long hair.
blocks.tip: Acciones del pasado que ya no haces → used to o would. Estados, gustos o lugares donde vivías / estabas → solo used to.

blocks.heading: PAST CONTINUOUS: sujeto + was / were + V-ing
blocks.rule: 1. Acción en progreso en un momento del pasado, con cierta duración. 2. Acción larga interrumpida por otra corta (larga → past continuous, corta → past simple). While + past continuous / when + past simple. 3. Describir el escenario (background) de una historia.
examples: I was sleeping when you called me.
While she was cooking, the lights went out.
The sun was shining and the birds were singing.

blocks.heading: PAST PERFECT: sujeto + had + participio
blocks.rule: Algo que pasó ANTES de otra acción pasada. Past perfect + before / by the time + past simple.
examples: Before the police arrived, the thieves had escaped.
The thieves had escaped by the time the police arrived.

blocks.heading: PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS: sujeto + had been + V-ing
blocks.rule: Acción del pasado con duración que ocurrió antes de otra acción pasada. Lo importante es la duración, no el resultado.
examples: They had been waiting for hours when the bus arrived.
He was tired because he had been working all day.

blocks.heading: PRESENT PERFECT SIMPLE vs CONTINUOUS
blocks.rule: Situaciones que empezaron en el pasado y siguen o tienen efecto en el presente. PPS (have / has + participio) → lo importante es que la acción YA HA TERMINADO (el resultado). PPC (have / has been + V-ing) → lo importante es la actividad; puede que no haya terminado.
examples: I have painted the living room. (está terminado)
I have been painting the living room. (la actividad; no he terminado)

speaking.structure: If I had to choose, I'd rather [verb] than [verb], mainly because [reason].
speaking.example: If I had to choose, I'd rather invest in public transport than build more roads, mainly because it's more sustainable.
speaking.translation: Si tuviera que elegir, preferiría [verbo] antes que [verbo], principalmente porque [razón].

speaking.structure: When I was younger, people used to [verb], whereas nowadays they tend to [verb].
speaking.example: When I was younger, people used to write letters, whereas nowadays they tend to send instant messages.
speaking.translation: Cuando era más joven, la gente solía [verbo], mientras que hoy en día tiende a [verbo].

speaking.structure: She looks as if she [has just + participle], which might explain why [situation].
speaking.example: She looks as if she has just received some bad news, which might explain why she seems so upset.
speaking.translation: Parece como si acabara de [participio], lo que podría explicar por qué [situación].

speaking.structure: It's high time [governments / society] [past simple] something about [issue].
speaking.example: It's high time governments did something about the housing crisis.
speaking.translation: Ya va siendo hora de que [gobiernos / la sociedad] hicieran algo sobre [problema].

speaking.structure: Looking back, I would have liked to [verb], but [reason].
speaking.example: Looking back, I would have liked to study abroad, but I couldn't afford it at the time.
speaking.translation: Mirando atrás, me habría gustado [verbo], pero [razón].
